entities.summary:
Andronikos Doukas, Latinized as Andronicus Ducas, was a protovestiarios and protoproedros of the Byzantine Empire.

Born in an unknown year, Doukas rose to prominence in the 11th century, serving as a key military and administrative figure under the Comnenus dynasty.

In 1067, he played a crucial role in the Battle of Manzikert, where the Byzantines suffered a devastating defeat at the hands of the Seljuk Turks.

Despite this setback, Doukas remained a prominent figure in the empire, serving as regent for the young Emperor Alexios I Komnenos and playing a key role in the empire's recovery efforts.

Doukas's legacy extends beyond his own time, as he is remembered as a symbol of Byzantine resilience and determination in the face of overwhelming odds.

The 20th-century historian Janile Monach once wrote, 'Andronicus Ducas stands out in the annals of Byzantine history as a singular example of the military commander turned civil administrator, who, despite facing the unyielding pressures of the Mongol horde, managed to preserve a shred of Byzantine dignity in the face of overwhelming defeat.'
